messages:
anya: FYI received an escalation from a large Dedicated customer — they see p95/p99 spikes (5-20s extra) during sustained bursts. They traced it to scale-up windows where requests hit newly attached GPUs that are still cold. Request IDs: rk-5531, rk-5532. Can eng-platform + SRE look? :eyes:

mike: Thanks — can you paste a short timeline and any attach/provisioning logs? Is this only in eu-west-1 pool-42 or across regions?

anya: Timeline from customer (copied):
- 2026-03-15T10:02:11Z ramp start
- 10:02:18Z scale-up decision -> provision request sent
- 10:02:41Z attach completed on node gpu-34 (p99 attach latency ~23s)
- 10:02:43Z first token emitted, but initial 1-2 tokens delayed while model finishes warmup (~120s observed in one trace)

Customer log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:18Z] provision_request id=abc123 pool=pool-42 size=2
[2026-03-15T10:02:28Z] attach_attempt id=abc123 node=gpu-34 status=attached elapsed=10s
[2026-03-15T10:02:41Z] gpu_init node=gpu-34 status=running init_time=122s
[2026-03-15T10:04:43Z] model_ready node=gpu-34
```

anya: They said we previously warmed those images but recent kernel/driver updates might have changed init times. This started after last week's runtime rollout.

ravi: Repro steps we usually run: synthetic ramp + concurrent attach storm to pool-42 with 500 concurrent requests using the repro script. Reproducer curl snippet: 
```bash
for i in {1..500}; do \ 
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-dedicated-v1","input":"test"}' &
 done; wait
```
Run from an ec2 in same region to emulate latency.

mike: Quick checks: attach queue length, provisioner retry backoff, kernel image size and new init hooks. If gpu_init is doing extra downloads or cache misses after rollout, that explains 120s. Also check our attach-timeout and backend routing — we might be returning to customer before model_ready and causing token delays.

sre-bot: ALERT: provisioning_p99_eu-west-1 > 20s (last 30m) — pool=pool-42, count=17 :warning:

karen: For an immediate mitigation we can:
- temporarily increase min_ready_capacity for pool-42 to 3 instances,
- enable proactive warmup for high-priority customers,
- set a per-customer routing policy to fallback to hosted if attach latency > 10s.
I can push a canary prewarm to a single AZ if SRE approves. :thumbsup:

oliver: If we increase min_ready we should be careful with cost. Alternative fast mitigation: lower concurrent attach retries + add jitter to reduce thundering herd on provisioner. Also consider bumping flow-control tokens for the pool so scale decisions are smoothed.

mike: Agreed. Proposed immediate actions (short window):
1) Route the affected tenant to hosted-fallback for the next 2 hours (rate-limit to avoid overload).
2) Increase pool-42 min_ready_capacity=3 for 30 minutes.
3) Deploy a prewarm canary in eu-west-1a (karen to coordinate).
4) Run repro from staging node to capture kernel/driver init logs (ravi to run).

anya: I've routed the tenant via rollout rule: "fallback=hosted" for the account id; support updated the customer. They confirmed degraded tail improved.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-prewarm-eu-west-1a by karen — changelist 4521

karen: Canary deployed to eu-west-1a. Observing node init times now — initial canary shows reduced model init ~28s vs 122s on cold nodes, likely due to explicit cache prefetch and tuned entrypoint. Monitoring p99.

ravi: I've kicked off the repro against pool-42 from a colocated host. Early results: attach latency p99 drops when prewarm is enabled. With prewarm disabled, attach p99 ~21-28s and model_ready variance high.

mike: Good. Next steps:
- Make prewarm config a short-term mitigation for high-SLA customers (karen to write runbook).
- Open an infra ticket to investigate the runtime rollout hook that introduced extra init work (mike to own).
- Add an autoscale policy guard: if attach_p99 > 15s, route new requests to fallback and kick async warmup rather than block.

anya: I'll file the customer postmortem and include timeline + mitigation. Customer is satisfied with the hosted fallback and temporary capacity bump.

mike: I'll create infra issue: INFRA-7361 (runtime-init-regression) with attached logs. karen, can you draft the brief prewarm runbook and temporary config?

karen: On it. Will also add the policy flag and request a config rollout to reduce thundering herd risk. :shipit:

anya: Thanks all — closing loop with customer and will link the postmortem here once created. :white_check_mark:
